narration.say: No mobile signal, and you need help.
How can a text still reach rescuers?
With a supported phone and country, it goes via satellite.
Your phone sends a short text up to a satellite,
cues: a short text up to a satellite,

narration.say: which passes it down to a ground station, then to a response centre.
Unlike a nearby tower, the satellite is far away: aim at open sky, expect slower replies.
Try the demo before going off-grid.
Follow Media Diet for technology explained.

shots.name: valley, low: tower signal rings stop at the ridge; phone shows no signal; question tag; tilt up to the empty sky
3/4 medium: paper satellite glides in along its arc; phone switches to satellite mode and leans to aim
low at the phone: the short text (paper bubble) lifts off and rises along the uplink to the satellite
low at the ground station: dish turns to the satellite; the text comes down to it
high 3/4: the text runs along the route to the response centre; windows light, SOS placard flips up
crane: nearby tower's small coverage circle, then up the long thread to the distant satellite
medium: under the tree the link is blocked; phone moves to open sky; slow reply descends (stopwatch)
trailhead close: practice demo on the phone completes with a check; off-grid signpost swings up
hero pull-back over the whole route + Media Diet paper sign (CTA)
